steps.note: One step, producing a Draft. No fine accrues without an approved policy that is live — a policy in draft or awaiting approval fines nobody (BR-2).

operations.name: fee.latefee.policy.create
operations.idempotencyKey: effective_from + branch_id, since one policy version takes effect per date
operations.purpose: Create a draft stepped late fee policy with its charges, its ages and its cap.

parameters.name: steps
parameters.notes: The series of steps, each with a step number, the days past the due date it applies at, a charge type and its value. Each step applies at more days than the one before (BR-4, E1), and each adds its own charge on top of the previous one (BR-3). Every figure comes from the request — nobody types a penalty at the desk, but somebody does set the policy.

parameters.name: cap_per_invoice
parameters.notes: The most the fines on one invoice may total. Only where the request states one — without a cap a small debt grows without limit, which no school intends (BR-8), so its absence is worth reporting.

parameters.name: applies_to
parameters.type: enum: All fee types | Selected fee types
parameters.notes: Which fee types the policy fines.

parameters.name: fee_type_ids
parameters.notes: Required where applies_to is Selected fee types.

parameters.name: effective_from
parameters.notes: The date the policy applies from. It does not fine invoices whose steps were passed before it existed (BR-6).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: policy_id
fields.description: The policy.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Draft. Nothing accrues against it (BR-2).

fields.name: version
fields.description: Incremented from any earlier approved policy.

fields.name: steps
fields.description: step_number, days_after_due_date, charge_type, amount or percentage.

fields.name: cap_per_invoice
fields.description: Absent where none was set — report that (BR-8).

fields.name: worked_example
fields.description: What a PKR 5,000 invoice would accrue at each step, so the policy can be read before it is agreed.

errors.meaning: A step applies at the same age as, or earlier than, the one before it.
errors.note: Two steps at the same age is a policy nobody can explain (BR-4).

errors.meaning: A step carries a charge of zero or less.

planningRules.rule: Never invent a step, a charge or an age. This is what every late-paying family in the school will be fined, and a figure a planner supplied becomes a penalty nobody agreed.
Report when no cap is set. Without one a small debt grows without limit, which no school intends (BR-8) — its absence is a decision, and usually an oversight.
Never describe a draft policy as active. No fine accrues without an approved policy that is live (BR-2); a draft fines nobody, and a school that thinks it has a policy running has not.
Never chain the approval. Setting a penalty and agreeing to it are separate acts by separate people (BR-5).
Never offer to apply the policy to past invoices. It applies from its effective date and does not reach back (BR-6).

reversal.statement: A draft is not deleted — the lifecycle runs Draft, Awaiting approval, Approved, Returned, Superseded. An unwanted draft is simply not submitted, and a policy that changes is superseded by a new version. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

steps.note: One step. From the effective date fines apply automatically as invoices age (BR-1, BR-2).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Whether the acting user built the policy themselves is enforced by the API and arrives as an error.
plan.atomicity: One write: the decision, the status change and the audit entry together or not at all. Approving makes the policy live; from its effective date fines accrue automatically, each as its own line on the invoice rather than folded into the original amount (BR-7), and each posting to the late fee income account separately from fee income (BR-13). It does not reach back to invoices whose steps were passed before it existed (BR-6). Any earlier approved policy is superseded.

fields.description: The School Admin, who may not be the person who built it (BR-5).

fields.description: How many outstanding invoices the policy will begin fining. Worth reporting before it goes live.

fields.name: retroactive
fields.description: Always false. The policy does not reach back (BR-6).

errors.meaning: Accounts attempted to approve their own policy.
errors.note: Setting a penalty and agreeing to it are separate acts by separate people (BR-5).

planningRules.rule: Never approve a policy the acting user built. E3 is BR-5 working — setting a penalty and agreeing to it are separate acts.
Report how many outstanding invoices the policy will begin fining. It goes live and starts charging families automatically (BR-1), and the number is what makes that concrete before it happens.
Never describe the policy as reaching back. It applies from its effective date and does not fine invoices whose steps were passed before it existed (BR-6).

reversal.statement: An approved policy is not withdrawn. It is superseded by a new version with its own effective date, and the earlier one is kept so a fine charged under it stays explicable. Fines already applied are not removed by superseding — they are waived one at a time, with reasons. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

errors.meaning: A fine was waived with no reason.
errors.note: Message: "Give a reason for removing this fine." Ask; never compose one.

errors.meaning: The fine has already been paid.
errors.note: Message: "This fine has been paid. A refund is the route, not a waiver." The money is in — waiving it now would leave a payment sitting against nothing.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the waiver reason. A waiver granted at a counter is visible afterwards because of it (BR-10), and that visibility is the control — a fine removed with a planner's explanation is a fine removed with none.

Never waive fines in bulk. Each carries its own reason (BR-10), and one reason covering thirty families describes none of them. Where a whole class was fined in error, that is a policy question, not thirty waivers.
Never waive a fine that has been paid. E8 is the boundary — the money is in, and waiving it leaves a payment sitting against nothing. A refund is the route.
Never describe the fine as deleted. It and its removal both stay on the record (BR-10), which is what makes a pattern of waivers readable.

reversal.statement: A waiver is not undone. Where a fine should stand after all, the policy will not re-apply it — the step has passed. Both the fine and its waiver stay on the record. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.
